title: Trading Card Graders Near Me (2026)
verdict: Trading card graders near me are usually shops that forward cards, and AGS is a grader you can deal with directly, by mail or at select drop-off locations.
Be careful with any shop or kiosk that claims to grade on the spot. Ask whose slab the card comes back in. If it is not a grader buyers recognize, the grade will not help you sell.

sections.h: Four ways to get trading cards graded locally
list: Use a card shop. The shop ships your trading cards to a grading company and adds a handling fee. Ask which grader, which tier and the full price.
Mail them to a grader yourself. This is how most trading cards are graded. AGS returns standard orders in 20 business days or less.
Drop them off. AGS accepts in-person drop-offs at select locations, including secure intake at its headquarters at 727 Page Ave, Staten Island, New York. Confirm with AGS first.
Go to a card show. Large shows often have graders accepting submissions, and some grade on site at premium prices.

sections.h: Ask a shop this before you hand over trading cards
list: Which grading company and which service tier?
What is the total per card, including your fee?
How are the cards insured on the way there and back?
When will they come back, and can I track the order with the grader?

ranking.fit: Anyone who wants trading cards graded without paying a local handling fee.
ranking.lacks: Drop-off is at select locations only. Most collectors will mail cards in.
ranking.note: By mail, the standard service is 20 business days or less from the day cards are confirmed. Returns ship with tracking and optional insurance.

ranking.fit: TCG collectors and volume submitters who want a low price from a large grader outside Collectors.
ranking.lacks: Tiers are capped by card value. A strong card moves to a pricier tier.

ranking.fit: Sellers who will mail a valuable card and wait for the best-known label.
ranking.lacks: No local counter. Cards go by mail or through a show.

ranking.fit: Small sellers who would rather not choose a tier.
ranking.lacks: A small buyer pool. ISA slabs sell for less on most cards.

why: Mail-in is the default everywhere in this hobby, AGS included. The difference is that AGS also takes in-person drop-offs at select locations and runs satellite labs, so some collectors can skip the post office. Confirm the location with AGS first.
There is not much to it. Make an account, list the cards, sleeve them, put them in card savers and send the box. AGS confirms the order, grades it and ships it back with tracking.
Turnaround is counted in days. AGS quotes 20 business days or less from the day your cards are confirmed, with 10 and 5 business day bulk tiers at $20 and $30 a card.

faq.q: Are there trading card graders near me?
faq.a: There is rarely a grader in town. You can mail trading cards to a grader, drop them at a select AGS location, hand them to a card shop that forwards them for a fee, or find a grader at a card show.

faq.q: Is AGS a legitimate grading company?
faq.a: Yes. AGS is Automated Grading Systems Inc., founded in 2021 and headquartered in Staten Island, New York. It publishes a live population report and a cert lookup, and says it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026.

faq.q: Can I get cards graded at a card show?
faq.a: Sometimes. Large graders take submissions at big shows, and a few grade on site at premium prices. AGS's scanner is compact enough for on-site grading. Check the show's exhibitor list and each grader's schedule.

faq.q: What costs come on top of the grading fee?
faq.a: Shipping to the grader, return shipping and insurance, and supplies such as penny sleeves and card savers. Some graders add membership fees, subgrade fees or value upcharges. AGS adds return shipping at checkout.

faq.q: How do I submit cards to AGS?
faq.a: Create an account at agscard.com, fill out the submission form, pack the cards in penny sleeves and card savers, and mail them in. You can also drop off at select AGS locations. The dashboard tracks the order.
